ABOUT

Practice before puck drop.

Rinkside Clock is a free, independent place to learn hockey scoreboard controls before your shift at the rink.

Built around the equipment you actually use.

The simulators recreate documented hockey workflows and recognizable controller layouts. Guided lessons explain a sequence, Test yourself gives an outcome to achieve, and free practice lets you explore.

The project is maintained by David Cameron. Source code, corrections and change history are public on GitHub.

What “coverage” means here.

Twelve playable training profiles are supported by manuals, local guides and reference images. They are fixed training configurations, not complete hardware or firmware emulators. A manufacturer manual, a photographed hockey insert and a Canadian arena report establish different facts; we label them separately.

The directory is not a census of Canadian rinks. Evidence is strongest in Ontario, British Columbia and Alberta. Regional reports and unresolved models are tracked on the coverage page.

Rinkside Clock is not affiliated with the equipment manufacturers or a governing hockey organization. Simulator progress is practice feedback, not officiating certification.

Help improve the next shift.

Found a different insert, missing controller or incorrect sequence? Please include the model label, hockey overlay, manual link and arena name in a controller report. We verify evidence before treating a profile as a match.
